about: The Capabilities page's 'Fixed this week' strip (director steer, 24 Oct 2026). One row per fix a reader of that page would care about: the commit that made it and one plain sentence. The date is never written here: tools/generate_capabilities_door.py reads it from git at publish, keeps only the rows inside the window, and computes whether the published run already carries each fix. A row whose commit does not resolve stops the feed. Add the row in the commit after the fix lands; rows that have aged out may be deleted.

fixes.what: Standard-variable bills above the price cap: the last of three billing defects is fixed. An incoming occupant was priced as a business, the Energy Price Guarantee did not reach the household's bill, and an estimate on an empty home's stub charged the Treasury's share. The fall was graded on a fresh run in d909b6933; what remains is named there, not closed.
The Energy Price Guarantee reaches the household's bill from October 2022 to June 2023, and the Treasury's share is booked as the supplier's revenue.
A household moving into an empty home is billed as a home, not as a business.
A household on the default tariff pays one unit rate; a time-of-use pair now needs the household's choice, not just a smart meter.
A time-of-use bill prints its peak and off-peak registers, each with its own units, rate and charge.
The Energy Bills Support Scheme's monthly credit reduces what a household owes for electricity in winter 2022-23.
On this page, a function with no linked test can no longer read Live.
